title: Successful Pairs of Spells and Potions
summary: Given two arrays, spells and potions, where spells[i] is the strength of the i^th spell and potions[j] is the strength of the j^th potion, along with an integer success, determine the number of potions that will form a successful pair with each spell.
statement: Given two arrays, spells and potions, where spells[i] is the strength of the i^th spell and potions[j] is the strength of the j^th potion, along with an integer success, determine the number of potions that will form a successful pair with each spell. A pair is successful if the product of the spell's strength and the potion's strength is at least equal to the success value. Return an array of length n, where each element represents the count of successful pairs for the corresponding spell.
constraints: A spell-potion pair succeeds when their positive strength product is at least success.
Return one count for each spell in original order.
Potions may be reordered for searching but duplicate potion values count separately.
reference_solution:
def successful_spell_potion_counts(spells,potions,success):
    from bisect import bisect_left
    ordered=sorted(potions);count=len(ordered);answer=[]
    for spell in spells:
        required=(success+spell-1)//spell
        answer.append(count-bisect_left(ordered,required))
    return answer
